comments.title: Why You Can't Stand On Jupiter
comments.question: Galileo never found a floor. How far down do you think Orbit would get before turning back?
How long do Saturn's rings have left?

comments.title: What Happened to Venus?
comments.question: Venus started like Earth: same size, same rock. It lost its water and kept its carbon dioxide in the air. Do you think Venus ever had oceans, or did the steam never come down? Tell me why.

comments.title: What Happens If You Travel Near Light Speed?
comments.question: Near light speed your own clock slows: one year on board, seven years at home. Would you take a trip that costs you seven years at home for one of yours? Tell me why.

Opportunity was built for ninety days on Mars and kept going for more than fourteen years. If you could send one robot to Mars, would you give it solar panels and hope for the wind, or a nuclear heart that never goes dark? Tell me why.

comments.title: Space Documentary for Sleep: A Slow Journey From the Moon to Andromeda
comments.question: Where along this 108-minute drift — from the Moon and the quiet planets of the solar system out to Proxima Centauri, Betelgeuse, and the Andromeda galaxy — are you listening from tonight?

comments.title: How Far Is the Nearest Star? (You Can't See It, and It Has a Planet)
comments.question: Walking without a single stop, you would reach Proxima Centauri in about nine hundred million years. If you could send one thing there, a probe the weight of a paperclip or a radio hello that arrives in 2031, which would you pick? Tell me why.
